t:
(a) 
Section 1(d) of the Act of October 15, 1966 (42 U.S.C. 1900(d); 80 Stat. 951) is repealed.
 
    (b) 
The second paragraph under the heading “surveying the public lands” of the first section of the Act of March 2, 1895, entitled “An Act making appropriations for sundry civil expenses of the Government for the fiscal year ending June thirtieth, eighteen hundred and ninety-six, and for other purposes” (43 U.S.C. 886; 28 Stat. 937) is amended by striking out “, and the Secretary of the Interior shall report to each regular session of Congress what has been done under the foregoing provisions” in the last sentence thereof.
 
    (c) 
Section 1 of the Colorado River Storage Project Act (43 U.S.C. 620; 82 Stat. 897), is amended by striking out “Provided, That construction of the Uintah of the Central Utah project shall not be undertaken by the Secretary until he has completed a feasibility report on such unit and submitted such report to the Congress, along with his certification that, in his judgment, the benefits of such unit or segment will exceed the costs and that such unit is physically and financially feasible, and the Congress has authorized the appropriation of funds for the construction thereof:”.
 
    (d) 
Section 4(c) of the Act of September 7, 1964, entitled “An Act to provide for the construction of the Lower Teton division of the Teton Basin Federal reclamation project, Idaho, and for other purposes” (43 U.S.C. 616qq(c); 78 Stat. 926), is repealed.

fable.w: The section only repeals or strikes existing provisions, mainly requirements that the Secretary report or submit feasibility findings to Congress. The tempting reading is that reports and certifications to Congress are a form of consultation, but Congress is inside the federal government, and these requirements are being removed rather than created. Nothing here brings states, the public, experts, or any other outside party into a federal decision, and no rulemaking, hearing, advisory body, or right to sue is established.
fable.s: the Secretary of the Interior shall report to each regular session of Congress what has been done under the foregoing provisions

opus.w: This section only repeals or strikes earlier rules that required the Secretary to report to, or certify to, Congress. Reports to Congress stay inside the federal government, and here even those requirements are being removed. No one outside the federal government is consulted, heard or given a right to object or sue, so this is not participation despite its procedural wording.
opus.s: is amended by striking out ", and the Secretary of the Interior shall report to each regular session of Congress what has been done under the foregoing provisions"
opus.b: 1. **Thinking it through.** The tempting reading is that this section involves participation because it deals with reports, a feasibility certification and congressional authorization. It doesn't pass the definition. Every requirement mentioned involves only the Secretary of the Interior and Congress, both of which are inside the federal government. The section also repeals or strikes those requirements rather than creating any process. No state, tribe, expert, company or member of the public is involved.

qwen_chat.w: This section amends or repeals provisions related to reporting to Congress or internal feasibility studies. Congress is inside the federal government, so reporting to it is not participation. The text does not establish any new process for consulting with or coordinating with outside parties (such as states, tribes, or the public) before a federal decision is made.
qwen_chat.s: (b) The second paragraph under the heading “surveying the public lands” of the first section of the Act of March 2, 1895... is amended by striking out “, and the Secretary of the Interior shall report to each regular session of Congress what has been done under the foregoing provisions” in the last sentence thereof.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that repealing a requirement for the Secretary to submit a report to Congress (subsection b) or to submit a feasibility report to Congress before construction (subsection c) removes a form of "participation" or oversight. However, the definition explicitly states that reports to Congress are *not* participation because Congress is inside the federal government. Therefore, removing such a requirement does not create participation, nor does the text describe any new process involving outside parties. The text is purely about amending or repealing existing statutory provisions regarding internal government procedures or funding authorizations.
